PullRequest.Title: mcp: Activate lazy providers in Agent Customizations
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #327317

## Problem

Extension-contributed MCP providers are registered as uncached lazy collections with no initial server definitions. Opening **Agent Customizations > MCP Servers** refreshed the already-materialized server list but did not activate those collections, so the provider extension remained inactive and its servers were absent.

Running another discovery command such as **MCP: List Servers** activated the same provider and made the server appear, which explains why reinstalling or interacting with the regular VS Code MCP surface temporarily repaired the Agent Customizations list.

## Change

Activate MCP collections when the MCP management section becomes visible and when MCP access is restored while that section is already visible.

Activation remains scoped to explicit user intent: this does not eagerly activate MCP providers during workbench startup. It is gated by MCP access, repeated visibility notifications remain idempotent, and provider activation failures are surfaced through the notification service.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `scripts/test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\mcpListWidget.test.js` — 43 passing
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check`
- Added coverage for:
  - activation on the first visible transition;
  - no activation while MCP access is disabled;
  - activation when access is restored while visible;
  - user-visible activation errors.
- Live Code OSS A/B with an isolated profile and a lazy extension-contributed MCP provider:
  - Unpatched: opening Agent Customizations left the provider inactive and the server absent; running **MCP: List Servers** activated it and made the server appear.
  - Patched: opening the MCP section activated the provider immediately and showed the server before any discovery command was run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Agent Customizations > MCP Servers for the first time with MCP access enabled and one or more uncached extension-contributed collections
Scenarios.CriticalPath: McpListWidget.setVisible(true) synchronously starts activateCollections and refresh, but both promises are deliberately fire-and-forget, so neither extension activation nor gallery loading must complete before the section can render its current state. Provider results arrive through the MCP service observable and trigger a later refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate each extension-contributed MCP collection through IExtensionService.activateByEvent, then wait for initial provider publication promises
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lazy load per allowed uncached collection U, launched concurrently by McpRegistry.discoverCollections via Promise.all; multiple collections from an already-activating extension may be internally coalesced by the extension service, but no registry-level grouping by extension is established.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening this section did not activate lazy MCP provider extensions; activation occurred only on other explicit MCP discovery paths such as MCP: List Servers or autostart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced on this scenario by the diff, but off the section's blocking critical path because the added call is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active snapshot query for the visible empty-query state, guarded by snapshot/loading/failure state and cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same setVisible refresh already initiated gallery snapshot loading before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Also fire-and-forget from setVisible; it updates the list later and is not added or increased by the activation change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U, the number of allowed uncached lazy MCP collections, controls extension activation fan-out; S, the number of discovered server definitions, controls the subsequent reconciliation (including an existing O(S^2) matching loop). Typical effective U is the user's installed MCP-provider collection count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All U uncached collection loads run concurrently through Promise.all. The gallery request may overlap with activation. There is no new UI-thread await or serialized queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only collections with lazy.isCached === false are activated. Successful providers replace their lazy collection with a non-lazy collection; providers that publish nothing are removed, so later discovery has no provider boundary. Cached lazy collections are excluded by existing registry semantics.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added call path, fire-and-forget placement, Promise.all fan-out, and lazy-collection cache transition based on the changed hunk and registry/discovery implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension activation cost and installed provider count vary, and arbitrary extension activation work is not measurable from this diff. The concrete fan-out is generally small and user-initiated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new work is the required explicit-user-intent discovery, remains off the render-blocking critical path, and is bounded to uncached collections rather than startup or every refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Leave and later re-enter the MCP Servers section after collection discovery completed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each false-to-true visibility transition calls activateCollections and refresh. discoverCollections finds no uncached collections, resolves immediately, and updateCollectedServers reconciles the already materialized definitions; setVisible still does not await it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero after successful discovery because no uncached lazy collections remain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No activation attempt was made from section re-entry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the MCP gallery snapshot if it is still absent and eligible
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally zero with a warm snapshot; existing state guards bound it to one active request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh and cache guards ran on every visible transition.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Section navigation frequency R and server count S; the added warm activation wrapper performs registry filtering plus existing server reconciliation per re-entry, with matching cost up to O(S^2).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No provider work after successful discovery. The activation promise and refresh are independently scheduled, but warm activation completes after an empty Promise.all and performs one reconciliation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful or empty uncached providers are transitioned out of the unknown set. Gallery snapshot state is retained by the widget. There is no new retained cache or key growth.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that warm transitions invoke reconciliation but do not cross the extension-host activation boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large MCP server counts are not established as realistic, and the reconciliation avoids observable writes when server identities/order are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the diff adds repeated warm reconciliation, realistic server cardinality and unchanged observable output do not establish a concrete user-visible regression rather than a minor optimization opportunity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore MCP access while the MCP section is already visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: updateAccessState starts provider activation and then immediately starts the pre-existing search query or refresh; neither is awaited by the configuration event handler. The disabled UI can be removed without waiting for providers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate allowed uncached extension MCP collections and await initial provider publications
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent load per allowed uncached collection U; zero once collections have previously been discovered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restoring access only restarted the current gallery search or local refresh; lazy provider extensions remained inactive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced by the diff but asynchronous and off the configuration handler's blocking critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run one MCP gallery search for a non-empty query, or load one eligible gallery snapshot for an empty query
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One current query, with existing cancellation/loading guards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same query-or-refresh branch existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May overlap with provider activation but was already triggered by access restoration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U uncached lazy collections and, independently, one current gallery query; access restoration is an infrequent user or policy/configuration event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider loads fan out with Promise.all and can overlap the existing single gallery operation. No new limiter exists, but the trigger is explicit/infrequent and collections are cache-bounded.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: While access is disabled the public registry view is empty but underlying lazy registrations persist. On restoration only uncached unknown collections load; subsequent restorations after successful discovery have no provider IPC.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the configuration listener, access-state branch, asynchronous scheduling, and cache behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The extension activation burden varies by provider, but the event frequency and uncached-state transition bound repeated impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new boundary is necessary to repopulate the visible section after access restoration, is not awaited, and does not recur after successful discovery.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and every diff hunk for the performance focus. Traced visibility and access-state callers through MCP registry discovery, extension-host activation, server reconciliation, observable refresh, and gallery network paths. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; no regression-fix learning signal applies.
